 Macklin Celebrini, Will Smith credit ‘roommate chemistry' for Sharks' win 
 "Roommate chemistry" was at an all-time high as Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith each scored in the San Jose Sharks' win over the Nashville Predators. 
 By Kevin Topley • 
 Published November 15, 2026 • 
 Updated on November 15, 2026 at 10:15 pm 
 BOOKMARKER 
 Share 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith join “Sharks Postgame Live” after San Jose’s 4-2 win over the Nashville Predators on Sunday at SAP Center. 
 Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith might be the best roommate duo in the NHL. On Sunday night, it showed for the Sharks.
 The team's top line of Ivar Stenberg, Celebrini and Smith combined for eight points, and each scored a goal, in a 4-2 win over the Predators at SAP Center, snapping Nashville's seven-game winning streak.
 Smith and Celebrini each had a goal and two assists, and Stenberg had a goal and an assist. Smith also scored his 50th career goal in the game, making him the fifth-fastest Shark to get there.

 Asked on "Sharks Postgame Live" with NBC Sports California’s Drew Remenda what got the line going, Celebrini kept it simple.
 "We just played, three skilled players on a line, you're just gonna play," Celebrini said.
 Asked how the chemistry works on the ice, Smith, smiling, credited what happens off it.
 "Yeah, we were trying to get it going, but I guess it's that roommate chemistry," Smith said.

 The best example of that roommate chemsitry came late in the game. Celebrini's goal at 7:40 of the third period was a product of that. Celebrini passed across the ice to Smith, skated into the slot and scored off Smith's no-look return pass, and he said he knew the puck was coming back.
 "He's a passer and he's got great vision, so once he didn't shoot it right away, figured he was coming back," Celebrini said.
 WILLMACK GOAL 🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨 pic.twitter.com/RruwvjBuUi 
— Sharks on NBCS (@NBCSSharks) November 16, 2026 
 Celebrini said the Sharks won because they stopped overthinking it.
 "We weren't second-guessing ourselves, we were playing fast, and I mean, that's our game," Celebrini told reporters after the game.
 After needing a shootout in Utah on Saturday, Celebrini said the group is starting to come together.
 "I think we're just starting to gel. I mean, we're talking more, we're skating and we're supporting each other, which is what we need to do," Celebrini said.
 The line is a big part of that. Celebrini, who has 11 points in his last seven games, said having Stenberg and Smith beside him opens things up.
 "It's been a lot of fun. We're making a lot of good plays, and, I mean, with those two, it's just the more we have the puck, the more chances we can create," Celebrini said.
 A product of the line having fun came on the first goal of the game at 12:25 of the first period. Eric Pohlkamp picked up a loose puck and rimmed it to Celebrini, who lobbed it ahead for a two-on-one. Stenberg won the race to the loose puck with a diving effort and fed Smith, who finished the breakaway.
 CAN'T TEACH THAT 😤 pic.twitter.com/IqotjO77H4 
— Sharks on NBCS (@NBCSSharks) November 16, 2026 
 Celebrini said Stenberg is a big part of why the line works.
 "He's just so smart, his puck handling and his vision. I think you see just how poised he is with the puck and how much patience, but also he knows when to make the play, which is fun to play with and fun to be on the line with," Celebrini said.
 Smitty returns the favor for Ivar 🙌 pic.twitter.com/cAH4YN41Mh 
— Sharks on NBCS (@NBCSSharks) November 16, 2026 
 The goaltending mattered too. Alex Nedeljkovic was a brick wall, as he made 32 saves on 34 shots in net, with Yaroslav Askarov resting after three straight shootouts, and Celebrini voiced that the Sharks needed him.
 "He was unbelievable. We played a much better defensive game, but there were stretches where we needed him, and he was there," Celebrini said.
 The win moved San Jose to 10-11-2, and the Sharks host the Calgary Flames on Tuesday with a line that looks like it is having fun, and more importantly clicking.
